title: You, Who Love a Phantom Love...
text:
You, who love a phantom love

and give a name to the mist,

to the ash of dreams...


You, who bend over yourself

as the willow bends

over its shadow reflected

in the water... You, who close

your empty arms over your

breast and murmur the word

no one hears, come and teach me

to pierce silence,

to kindle, to burn solitude...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the speaker asking a fellow lover of absence to teach her how to burn solitude.

title: To the One with the Saddest Love
text:
You, who love a phantom love

and give a name to the mist,

to the ash of dreams...


You, who bend over yourself

as the willow bends

over its shadow reflected

in the water...


You, who close

your empty arms over your

breast and murmur the word

no one hears, come and teach me

to pierce silence,

to kindle, to burn solitude...
editorial_note: The translation preserves this variant's title and stanza break in the ghost-love address.

title: Shipwreck
text:
Ah, what a swimming of soul this sea is!

What shipwrecked rowing of arms, what sinking

and coming afloat and sinking again!

Ah, what a sea without shores or horizon,

nor any ship to wait for! And what a clutching

at this soft darkness, at this void

that turns and turns... At this

black water slipping through the fingers...

What swallowing of salt and death in this

infinite absence of you!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the shipwreck as a bodily swimming through absence, salt, and death.

title: I Went On Undressing You...
text:
I went on undressing you of yourself,

of the superimposed "yous" that life

had fitted around you...


I tore away the bark-whole and hard-

that believed itself fruit, that had

the shape of fruit.


And before the vague astonishment of your eyes

you emerged with your eyes still veiled

in darkness and astonishments...


You emerged from yourself; from your own

fertile shadow-intact and torn

into living soul...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the stripping away of false selves until the living soul emerges.

title: I Went On Undressing You of Yourself...
text:
I went on undressing you of yourself...

I went on

        undressing you of yourself,

of the superimposed "yous" that life

had

        fitted around you...

I tore away the

        bark-whole and hard-

that believed itself fruit, that had

the shape of

        fruit.

And before the

        vague astonishment of your eyes

you emerged with your eyes still veiled

in

        darkness and astonishments...

You emerged from

        yourself; from your own

fertile shadow, intact and torn

into living

        soul...
editorial_note: The source catalog title says 'Hidden Water,' but the visible body is a broken-spaced variant of 'Yo te fui desnudando...'.
